title: 2027 Automation & Process Analytics Technology Co-Op (June - Dec)
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Envision working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie’s Co-Ops.  This is a work experience and is not intended to support a thesis.
Product Development Science and Technology (PDS&T): Designs, delivers, and supports biologics manufacturing processes for AbbVie’s pipeline and partnered products through clinical development and commercial life cycle. The department advances targeted product quality, CMC acceleration, people development, and efficient workflows, bringing together expertise across Cell Line Development, Cell Culture Process Development, Purification Process Development, Scale-Up Lab, and Analytical Development.
We are seeking an exceptional graduate co-op student to join our Cell Culture Development and Automation team for an innovative, hands-on project at the intersection of optical spectroscopy, cell culture science, laboratory robotics, and data analytics. In this role, you will help integrate spectroscopy with automated liquid-handling robotics to enable rapid, at-line characterization of cell-culture product quality and metabolites. You will have the opportunity to build novel hardware, develop automated analytical workflows, and apply chemometric and data-science modeling to production-relevant datasets, helping transform how process development teams learn from experiments.
Key responsibilities include:
Supporting integration of spectroscopy systems with an automated liquid-handling platform for high-throughput, at-line spectral acquisition from cell culture samples.
Designing and 3D printing custom labware and sampling components to support automated sample transfer and spectral measurement.
Developing and troubleshoot automated liquid-handler methods for sample acquisition, flow-cell delivery, and system wash and cleaning cycles.
Performing aseptic cell culture techniques, including thawing, passaging, and banking of mammalian (CHO) cell lines, to support experimental studies.
Collecting, processing, and analyzing Raman spectral and process data; apply chemometric and data-science techniques to build predictive models for metabolites and product quality attributes.
Collaborating cross-functionally with scientists in cell culture development, automation engineering, and analytical development to refine workflows using experimental results and team feedback.
Documenting experimental methods, data, and results clearly; contribute to a final presentation and/or manuscript-quality summary suitable for internal or external scientific communication.
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a Master’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Biochemical Engineering, Bioengineering, Chemistry or a related field.
Must be enrolled in university at the time of the Co-Op.
Expected graduation date between May 2028 – Dec 2028
Proficient in aseptic techniques, including thawing, passaging, and banking mammalian cell lines in a biosafety cabinet.
Knowledge of optical spectroscopy techniques, including Raman, fluorescence, and absorbance.
Knowledge of biology and biochemistry, cell metabolism, and protein characterization as applied to CHO cell culture development.
Must be able to commit to a 6-month program at AbbVie’s site located in Worcester, MA (June - December).
Preferred Qualifications
Strong critical-thinking skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex laboratory robotics and instrumentation challenges.
Ability to design and create custom labware using 3D printing.
Ability to execute, troubleshoot, and interpret complex experimental data to determine thoughtful next steps.
Working knowledge of programming or scripting languages such as Python, Visual Basic and C/C++.

Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings

Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or other related field

Preferred Qualifications
Exposure to comminution processes
Experience with physical characterization techniques (flowability, adhesion, cohesion, bulk density, laser diffraction particle size determination)

Partnering with study teams to drive the implementation of the aggressive execution strategies

Experience/exposure to drug development, operations, risk management, successful decision-making, strategic execution, in a fast-paced environment.

Targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNPs) represent a key new modality to enable effective delivery of mRNA. The tLNP chemistry, manufacturing, and control (CMC) team (TCT) is a newly formed group under Biologics CMC, Development Sciences, R&D. TCT focuses on process development for tLNPs, including mRNA process development, tLNP process development, and formulation development.
The tLNP Process Development team is seeking a highly motivated, talented, and innovative scientist with expertise in mRNA-LNP process development and an interest in laboratory automation. This team is responsible for the end-to-end manufacturing process from purified mRNA to purified tLNP bulk drug product, including encapsulating mRNA with lipid components to form LNPs, conjugating LNPs with a targeting moiety, and purifying the final tLNPs via tangential flow filtration (TFF).
The successful candidate will help advance fundamental understanding of tLNP unit operations, such as mRNA encapsulation, bioconjugation, and TFF, as well as scaling up lab processes into pre-clinical, clinical, and commercial scale manufacturing processes. The candidate will also apply automation expertise to integrate off-the-shelf and custom-built hardware, software, and data workflows into flexible experimental platforms that increase throughput, reproducibility, and process understanding.
The end goal for tLNP Process Development team is to deliver a robust manufacturing process at commercial scale. This includes science-based, hands-on approaches in the lab to optimize process parameters and understand the impact of process parameters on critical quality attributes. First-principle-based and statistical modeling will be applied where appropriate. Along the pharmaceutical development life cycle, the team will be responsible for successful production of non-GMP pre-clinical safety study supplies and GMP clinical study supplies from a manufacturing plant on site or at third party manufacturers. The team will also lead the tech transfer of commercial processes into a commercial facility. Additionally, the team reviews appropriate sections of Common Technical Document (CTD) for regulatory submissions.
Success in this role depends on close collaboration with the mRNA process development, drug product development, and analytical development, digital and automation partners, as well as cross-functional partners across Biologics CMC and Synthetic Molecule CMC. The work directly advances cutting-edge mRNA-based therapeutics.
Responsibilities
Independently design, execute and interpret critical experiments to understand unit operations such as mRNA encapsulation, bioconjugation, and tangential flow filtration, and scale up these unit operations to commercial manufacturing batch size.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory research or method development, requiring minimal direction from supervisor.
May initiate new areas of investigation that are scientifically meaningful, reliable, and can be incorporated directly into a research or development program.
Demonstrates high proficiency across a wide range of technologies relevant to tLNP process development.
Formulate conclusions and design follow-on experiments based on multidisciplinary data.
Primary author of publications, presentations, regulatory documents and/or primary inventor of patents.
Proactively develop and implement innovative automation solutions (custom and off-the-shelf equipment).
Apply AI tools for structured data capture, analysis, and predictive modeling.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, and GMP compliance.
Direct mentorship of others.
BS, MS, or PhD degree in Chemistry, Material Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Bioengineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or equivalent.
Senior Scientist I :  BS with 10+ years', MS with 8+ years', and PhD with 0+ years' industry experience.
Scientist II : BS with 7+ years', MS with 5+ years' industry experience.
Experience with LNP mixing technology in an academic lab, or industry experience with LNP drug product process development. For mRNA encapsulation, experience with systems such as impinging jet, coaxial jet, or multi-inlet vortex mixer is required.
Possess thorough theoretical and practical understanding of mRNA encapsulation.
Experience with bioconjugation is required.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to answer scientific questions.
Demonstrated ability to learn, understand, and master new experimental techniques.
Ability to multitask and work within timelines.
Demonstrated scientific writing skills and strong verbal communication skills.
Preferred Experience
Experience scaling up LNP processes to gram-scale mRNA or above.
Prior experience with automating existing experimental setups as well as new automation equipment and ecosystems, such as Ignition.

title: Principal Product Manager, Freight Express, Amazon Supply Chain Services
description:
You're a Principal Product Manager with deep experience in freight, supply chain, or logistics product strategy within complex, rapidly scaling organizations. You've owned end-to-end product vision for a freight or transportation product at scale, and you have a track record of turning multi-leg, multi-modal networks into a single differentiated product that shippers choose. You excel where the problem spans air and ground operations, cross-border complexity, commercial strategy, and customer experience — and you bring the strategic judgment to define the right long-term bets while delivering near-term value.
You have strong analytical skills and are comfortable diving deep into lane economics, transit-time and connection reliability, first- and last-mile ground performance, international compliance and customs flow, and the cost and margin structure of an end-to-end freight product. You understand that this is not project management — this is setting the product direction for how Amazon Air Cargo moves freight from gateway to gateway, extends it into a true door-to-door experience, and connects international lanes into the domestic network across two regions.
High judgment is expected at the Principal bar: defining the product promise across air and ground legs, making trade-offs between operational feasibility and customer experience, deciding when to build versus influence a platform or operations team's roadmap, and influencing across operations, network, commercial, finance, compliance, and engineering teams — across the US and EU — without direct authority. You set strategy that other senior leaders and teams align to, you regularly engage with senior leadership to secure investment and drive high-stakes decisions, and you are relied on to be right a lot. You have a proven track record of building a freight or transportation product that became a durable competitive advantage.
Key job responsibilities
Product Strategy Across the Freight Express Journey — Own the end-to-end product strategy for Freight Express across three connected layers:
Gateway-to-gateway — the existing Amazon Air Cargo airport-to-airport experience, from booking through air movement to arrival.
End-to-end with ground — extend the product into a door-to-door experience by integrating first-mile and last-mile ground into a single, reliable freight offering.
International — enable international lanes to feed into the domestic Freight Express network, connecting cross-border origins into the end-to-end product. Define the product customer-back across all three, with a single coherent promise rather than a stack of disconnected legs.
Multi-Region Ownership (US & EU) — Own the Freight Express product experience across both the US and EU. Account for the regulatory, operational, and commercial differences between regions while holding a consistent product bar, and decide where the product converges across regions versus where it must adapt.
End-to-End Product Lifecycle & Quality Ownership — Own the full product cycle and the quality of the product at every stage:
Product definition & strategy — set the vision and translate it into clear, prioritized product requirements.
Capability enhancement — drive the roadmap of capabilities that close gaps across the air and ground legs and the international feed.
Performance measurement — instrument the product and define success metrics up front; measure actual performance against the product promise and the business case.
Quality improvement — identify quality gaps from the data (connection misses, ground exceptions, customs delays, failure modes) and drive the highest-impact improvements back into the product and network. Continuously evolve the product based on customer feedback, operational quality and cost, and P&L outcomes.
Cross-Team & Network Leadership — Lead product vision and execution across multi-org dependencies, driving alignment across air gateway operations, ground first/last-mile carriers, international and customs operations, commercial, and engineering. Translate hard operational constraints (gateway cutoffs, ground pickup/delivery timing, cross-border clearance) into a single recommended path and a product customers can rely on. Eliminate fragmented ownership and missed handoffs across the air-to-ground and international-to-domestic seams; own the build-vs-influence calls and ensure capabilities land in the right long-term home.
A day in the life
Set the strategic direction for the Freight Express product across teams — aligning air, ground, international, commercial, and engineering around one gateway-to-gateway-to-door product definition.
Deep dive into data (lane economics, connection and on-time performance, ground first/last-mile reliability, customs and cross-border delays, customer feedback) to shape the roadmap and decide where to invest for maximum reliability and margin impact.
Run the product cycle end to end — move initiatives from strategy to requirements to capability launch, then measure outcomes, surface quality gaps, and feed them back into the next iteration.
Partner with engineering and operations leaders across the US and EU to shape network and product design, ensuring the product scales and holds its service promise in both regions.
Unblock cross-org dependencies before they become escalations; frame program narratives for senior leadership — connecting network and product progress to business outcomes.
Spend time with Ops teams and in the network — air gateways and ground legs — to pressure-test whether the product performs for shippers in the real world.
What this takes

description:
Device Technologies (DT) provides the infrastructure that lets Amazon's operations teams provision, deploy, and manage the edge devices, robotics, and material-handling equipment they run on. - Move DT's core outcomes measurably forward: empowering builder teams to move fast on their own (self-service), returning devices to productive work quickly when they fail (availability), and lowering the cost to serve each site.
- Decide where AI, including agentic and generative capabilities, genuinely improves the product or the speed at which your team builds, and where it adds risk or complexity that isn't worth it.
- Define the metrics that tell you whether the product is working, instrument them, and use site-level data and operator feedback to decide what to build next.
A day in the life
No two days are the same, but most begin with data from the floor. You might start with overnight numbers from a site rollout: adoption, device health, ticket volume, and the questions they raise about what to prioritize next. By mid-morning you're in a design review, pushing engineering on whether a recovery flow holds up under the conditions of a live building. The afternoon is for writing: a PR/FAQ for a capability you want funded, or a document that works through a trade-off you need leadership to weigh in on. You end the day with your partners in operations and the application teams who build on DT, making sure what you're about to ship will land cleanly in the sites that depend on it.

title: Commissioning Engineer, Data Center Engineering
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.

4+ years of direct field experience executing or managing commissioning in a Hyperscale data center, mission-critical facility, heavy industrial environment or similar.
Working knowledge of large-scale electrical delivery systems (e.g., UPS, switchgear, generation) and mechanical cooling systems (e.g., chilled water plants, hydronics, CRAH/CRAC units).
Experience directing and or overseeing Level 3 (Pre-Functional), Level 4 (Functional Performance Testing), and Level 5 (Integrated Systems Testing) activities onsite.
Strong ability to read, interpret, and field-verify MEP drawing packages, Single-Line Diagrams, and Sequences of Operation (SOO).
Experience managing onsite vendors, contractors, or specialized testing firms.
Ability to work onsite daily at the assigned data center location.
Preferred qualifications: Previous experience operating as a dedicated onsite Cx Engineer or Resident Engineer for a major data center build or campus expansion.
Industry-recognized commissioning certifications such as Certified Commissioning Authority (CxA), Certified Commissioning Professional (CCP), or Building Commissioning Professional (BCxP).
Hands-on experience with commissioning management software platforms (such as CxAlloy, Facility Grid, or similar tools) for daily field tracking and issue management.
Practical field experience troubleshooting Building Automation Systems (BAS), Direct Digital Control (DDC), and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS).
Strong understanding of field safety standards (OSHA/NFPA 70E), MOP execution, and hazardous energy control.
Demonstrated track record of identifying field coordination clashes, resolving complex physical engineering challenges, and driving continuous improvement feedback to global engineering teams.
Proficiency with AI tools to enhance daily work — including AI-assisted summarization of field reports, automated parsing of submittals, and tracking punch-list data.

description:

IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.
Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale?
Imagine what you could do here. From individual facilities to a worldwide network, Infrastructure Services ensures the technology underneath everything works without question.
As a Critical Facilities Technician, you will address sophisticated topics that craft how we maintain and operate our facilities and generate ideas that push team members and senior leaders to expand the boundaries of innovation and technology. Critical Facilities Technicians are responsible for the safe, professional, and operationally sound manipulation of the systems, such as cooling and electrical, that support systems in high-availability, high-risk, or high-reliability environments.

title: Darwin Runtime Engineer, Core OS
description:
For the engineer who obsesses over the butterfly effect of a single line of code, there is no greater stage than Apple's Core OS! Core OS builds uncompromising, lightning-fast foundation that iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS stand upon. We don't just write software; we forge the soul of the machine, ensuring the operating system and the hardware breathe as one to create a seamless device identity.
At the center of it all is Darwin, the UNIX-like heartbeat of Apple's operating systems, spanning from the deepest levels of the kernel up through critical low-level user components. The Darwin Runtime team is seeking visionary engineers to push the boundaries of low-level system technologies. If you obsess over performance, security, and the massive cascading impact of your code, your life's best work is waiting for you here!
The Darwin Runtime team is responsible for the development and evolution of low-level user space libraries such as Grand Central Dispatch (GCD), Inter-Process Communication (IPC) technologies like XPC, pthread, and malloc, among others. The foundational libraries built by our team are the invisible engines powering the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and the groundbreaking Vision Pro. We want an engineer with the drive to operate autonomously, the hunger to master new domains, and the ambition to step into technical leadership. Here, your voice shapes the future. You will drive critical design discussions, elevate peers through code reviews, and push the boundaries across a spectrum of technologies. Our environment fosters a culture of deep technical innovation, massive autonomy, and true ownership.
Minimum qualifications: Passion for low-level system technologies
Fluency in the C programming language
6+ years of Experience with UNIX-like systems
System design and architecture skills
Strong understanding of operating system fundamentals like threading, synchronization primitives, inter-process communication, scheduling, and virtual memory
Excellent collaborative skills, with the ability to work with a team to design system architecture
BS or MS in Computer Science or equivalent degree
Preferred qualifications: Knowledge of operating system implementation, hardware architecture and assembly programming
Knowledge of Swift or Objective-C
Skilled at interface and/or API design
Experience with lldb or gdb
Experience using Gen AI tools for Software Development

Because when advertising is done right, it benefits everyone.

You will have a strong understanding of scalable approaches and thrive working in Agile environments. The ability to be a good, standout colleague under tight deadline constraints is key to success. As part of the data organization, we work at the cutting edge of data engineering, machine learning, and privacy at Apple's scale. Excellent collaborative skills

Experience with anomaly detection

History of driving reliability, efficiency, or cost improvements, and mentoring other engineers

title: Design Verification Engineer
description:
At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. Do you love working on challenges that no one has solved yet and changing the game? We have an opportunity for an outstandingly hardworking design verification engineer! As a member of our wide-ranging group, you will have the rare and extraordinary opportunity to craft upcoming products that will delight and encourage millions of Apple’s customers daily.
This role is for a DV engineer who will enable us to produce fully functional first silicon for IP designs. The responsibilities include all phases of pre-silicon verification including but not limited to: establishing DV methodology, test-plan development, verification environment development including stimulus and checkers, test-writing, debug, coverage, sign-off for RTL freeze and tape-out.
In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring bug-free first silicon for part of the SoC / IP and are encouraged to develop detailed test and coverage plans based on the micro-architecture. You are responsible for developing verification methodology suitable for the IP, ensuring a scalable and portable environment. You will get to develop verification environment, including all the respective components such as stimulus, checkers, assertions, trackers, coverage. A mindset to break the design is highly desirable.
Furthermore, you will develop verification plans for all features under your care, execute verification plans, including design bring-up, DV environment bring- up, regression enabling features, and debug of the test failures. You will also learn to develop block, IP and SoC level test-benches track and report DV progress using a variety of metrics, including bugs and coverage. You will also be expected to make use of LLM and related technologies to achieve efficient execution and improved quality.
Minimum qualifications: BS degree in technical subject area and a minimum 10 years relevant industry experience or equivalent.
Preferred qualifications: Deep knowledge of OOP, SystemVerilog and UVM
Deep knowledge in developing scalable and portable test-benches
Strong experience with verification methodologies and tools such as simulators, waveform viewers, Build and run automation, coverage collection, gate level simulations
Working experience using LLMs for efficiency and quality
Experience with power-aware (UPF) or similar verification methodology
Excellent knowledge of one of the scripting languages such as Python, Perl, TCL
Experience with serial protocols such as PCIe or USB, parallel protocol such as DDR is a plus but not required
Knowledge of formal verification methodology is a plus but not required
Knowledge of emulation for verification technologies is a plus but not required

Prior experience operating at senior manager level or above in a large-scale technology organization.
Proven track record delivering large-scale enterprise technology programs — spanning infrastructure, data systems, retail or sales technology, or AI/ML platforms — with measurable business or operational impact.

Apple TV Marketing is seeking a Director of Media to drive strategic leadership of our paid media campaigns in the US and internationally. This includes strategic direction and management of work across series, films, the Apple TV brand, sports, performance and partner media to grow our platform and business. This leader must be incredibly collaborative and cross-functional both internally with partner teams and externally with our agency and talent.
The ideal candidate has a demonstrated track record with managing large-scale paid media budgets to drive growth in an entertainment business in the US and internationally. This leader should be able to take big swings that put campaigns in the cultural zeitgeist and also to react and adapt in real time. This leader must be an innovative thinker who can put our titles and brand in the cultural zeitgeist, while also understanding the business metrics to create campaigns that result in subscriber acquisition, retention, and viewership.

Minimum of 5 years of people management experience, building and leading teams.
Expertise in working with analytics to showcase the results of paid media campaigns.

Proven experience in both manual testing/QA methodology and test automation development

Demonstrated ability in software development with a focus on tools and test automation

description:

title: Wireless Module Engineer
description:
Apple is where individual imaginations gather committing to the values that lead to great work. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other’s ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It’s the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you’ll do more than join something — you’ll add something. The Wireless Module Engineer (WME) is well-versed in multiple fields for wireless module development: RF design, packaging, product engineering (including yield analysis), ATE, and reliability engineering.
The Wireless Module Engineer (WME) is a highly motivated, self-driven technical lead responsible for driving the development of wireless modules from early architecture definition through mass-production ramp. This role requires strong cross-functional collaboration and the ability to deeply engage across a broad spectrum of technical domains including RF design, reliability, manufacturing test, supply chain, and system integration. The WME will initiate and lead early-phase RF architecture and specification discussions between internal engineering teams and Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly & Test (OSAT). They will ensure all OSATs comply with internal specification formats, review procedures, and approval workflows. The WME will drive the formal module design release process, establishing and reviewing checkpoints for schematics, PCB layout, electromagnetic/RF simulation results, design-for-manufacturability (DFM), test data readiness, and OSAT design feedback
In addition to communicating risks and priorities, the core responsibility of WME is to manage module integration and ATE test coverage at OSATs. WME will function as a general manager overseeing all aspects of ATE maturity preparation for hardware—such as load boards, daughter cards, sockets, and handlers—and software, firmware, module calibrations, GRR, and CPK/data analysis.
This role is expected to drive OSATs, set priorities, and collaborate closely with them to validate and approve the final ATE hardware and software integration, test coverage, and corresponding test limits, ensuring timely delivery of tested modules for product NPI builds. Following the NPI builds, WME will lead the failure analysis process with the OSATs and work with them to implement improvement activities, including enhancing ATE testers, optimizing software/firmware test time, and improving overall yield and retest rates. This role will involve traveling to international OSATs for Module & ATE bring up for 1-2 weeks before the product NPI builds. WME is expected to have a broad spectrum of technical depth to debug additional bring up issues during travel. For e.g. I2C & PCIe interface related issues. This team member will facilitate collaboration with multi-functional groups at Apple and define the test coverage. Typical test coverage includes but not limited to Open-Short & Continuity test, VCO calibration and test, TX/RX power calibration and test, RF packet test, EVM test, RX sensitivity test. They will collaborate closely with internal reliability engineering teams to translate expected product field-usage profiles into feasible and data-driven reliability test models for modules and components. This role supports multiple product lines within the Hardware Technology organization, ensuring technical excellence, risk visibility, and disciplined execution from early concept through manufacturing ramp.
Minimum qualifications: Minimum requirement of a bachelors degree
Strong RF fundamentals.
Proven track record for effective written/verbal communication, leading projects with self-motivation.
Preferred qualifications: Prefers 2 or more years of wireless module development experience from early concept to MP for consumer electronic devices.
Strong RF design background. Additional experience in packaging, product engineering, ATE, and reliability engineering is highly desirable.
Strong data analysis skills including yield analysis (Cpk), and retest rate analysis, required for data sheet closures.
Capable of working at both high-level theory and detailed hands-on execution.
Experienced in managing vendor teams and leading cross-time-zone meetings.
AI/ML experience with expertise in Data Analysis is a plus.
Very good communication skills, verbal and written, including the capability to drive meetings to make key decisions on wireless technologies.

title: Battery Modeling Engineer
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Battery Modeling Engineer, you’ll build the data and degradation models that tell us how our batteries age in the real world. You’ll combine software engineering, data science, and semi-empirical degradation modeling, turning telemetry from our fleet of deployed home batteries and data from cell-level testing into trusted datasets and models that predict capacity fade, resistance growth, and remaining useful life across the conditions our batteries actually see.

This is a hybrid role at the intersection of software, data science, and battery science. You’ll own degradation analytics end to end, from the pipelines and data models that make fleet and lab data trustworthy to the semi-empirical models and tools the rest of Base relies on, and you’ll help found and set up Base’s cell characterization lab. Your work will directly shape how we operate our fleet and plan for its long-term performance.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and validate semi-empirical degradation models (calendar and cycle aging, capacity fade, resistance growth) for the cells in our fleet.

 - Help found and set up Base’s cell characterization lab: define test plans, select equipment, and stand up the processes that generate reliable aging data.

 - Analyze fleet- and device-level data to understand how temperature, state of charge, and usage patterns drive degradation, and validate model predictions against real-world behavior.

 - Turn model outputs into tools and insights that engineering, fleet, and markets teams use to decide how our batteries are operated.

 - Write production-quality Python and SQL (or equivalent), with the tests, documentation, and monitoring that keep models trustworthy as the fleet grows and ages.

 - Track model history and communicate those changes effectively across the organization.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - A background in Chemistry or Battery Physics or a related field such as electrochemistry, materials science, or chemical engineering.

 - PhD in physics modeling or battery chemistry preferred.

 - A world-class ownership mindset: you own outcomes, not just tasks.

 - Hands-on experience with battery modeling, ideally semi-empirical or physics-informed degradation models for lithium-ion cells.

 - Strong software and data skills: proficiency in Python and SQL (or equivalent).

 - Familiarity with cell testing and characterization (cycling, HPPC, EIS, or similar), and excitement about building a lab from the ground up.

 - Nice to have: experience with field or fleet data from deployed energy storage, EVs, or consumer electronics.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Modeling team owns how we understand the health and performance of our battery fleet. Every battery we deploy is a long-lived asset, and how it ages determines how we operate it, how it supports the grid, and how much value it creates for our members over its life. As the fleet grows across more homes, climates, and operating conditions, that question gets harder and more valuable to answer. This team gets to build Base’s degradation modeling capability from the ground up, from a new cell characterization lab to models running on fleet-scale telemetry, so we can predict how our batteries will age and make better decisions about every battery in the field.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

Job Description:
What It Means to Be a Consultant at Crowe
Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. In this role, you will continuously learn, collaborate across teams, and explore how tools, including emerging AI capabilities, can improve efficiency, insights, and client outcomes.
As you grow, you’ll also begin to take ownership of client relationships, contribute to account strategy, and support the delivery of high-impact work. Developing a sense of account leadership, including understanding client needs, ensuring delivery excellence, and building trusted partnerships, is part of what sets successful consultants apart.
Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.
As Salesforce Consultant with Crowe, you will play a key role on our project team by bridging the gap between business problems and technical solutions for our clients. You will engage directly with customers to understand their needs, design custom solutions, deliver & implement innovative real-world solutions. You will be expected to provide consultative advice regarding industry best practices and create a solution that always best meets our client’s needs.
Key Responsibilities Include
Pre-sales scoping, supporting a Solution Architect/Sr. Consultant, as needed
Documenting business requirements, functional requirements & technical requirements in a pre-sales environment to generate a solution and Scope of Work, as needed
Work closely with key stakeholders (internal & client facing) to capture business needs, define requirements for the scoped work and clearly outline the affected business processes
Assist in fully solutioning scopes of work that meet business needs in a clear and cohesive manner, with oversight from SA/SC
Work at discretion of SA/SC for project implementation & architectural design by both solutioning and delivering on workstreams as identified & assigned
Assist in the creation of the Solution Design Documentation with the support of Technical and Solution Architect that includes but is not limited to: Detailed user stories and acceptance criteria
Entity Relationship Diagrams and Data dictionary
Current state and future state process flows
Wireframes and mockups
Use declarative functionality to build solutions & complete all assigned project actions using Salesforce and Crowe best practices
Assist in project delivery once work is completed by completing QA of all work, compiling change sets for deployment & assist in building all documentation for the client
As you continue to grow in your role and work further towards becoming a more independent consultant, you will lead smaller projects on your own from end to end with oversight from SA/SC

Our ideal candidate will possess the following skills
Competency & experience with Salesforce core products
Drive and desire to learn and grow both technical and functional skill sets and expand knowledge of the Salesforce platform
2+ years’ minimum experience on the Salesforce platform
Experience managing & delivering multiple projects at the same time
Detail-oriented, enthusiastic, self-starter with ability to work both independently and in a team environment
Strong, dynamic communication skills - both written & verbal - with ability to work cross-functionally and speak to members at any level of an organization (both client & prospect)
Ability to log time on a daily basis for client and project reporting needs
Positive minded, solutions-oriented approach and outlook is critical
Ability to work - and thrive - in a fast-paced, high-growth, innovative environment
This position requires a minimum of 20% travel
Bachelor’s degree

Willingness to obtain Certification in Salesforce Admin and one of the Consulting Cloud certifications.

About the Role
The Sort Capacity Manager owns network-wide capacity de-risking for the Sort organization. This role builds and maintains the constraint model that defines what “de-risked capacity” means across every 1P and 3P facility — dock door availability, floor/pallet-position space, max throughput, and optimal labor and automation.
About the Team
Own the network constraint model — Model site capacity against its underlying constraints: dock door availability (inbound/outbound truck cadence by hour, translated from Mx forecast), floor/pallet-position space (inbound-to-outbound hourly volume vs. staging capacity), max throughput (automation vs. manual sortation rate, package profile mix, cross-dock vs. sort), and optimal labor hours required to hit max output.
Govern spoke capacity data — Drive spoke capacity maintenance in the sort app, ensuring product reflects current facility configuration, and hold cross-functional partners accountable when it doesn't.
Own zip-to-facility strategy — Own zip code-to-facility mapping and re-optimization as volume and rates shift, balancing service-level and cost trade-offs.
Own device and consumable readiness — Forecast scanners, bins, and gaylords against site growth to avoid reactive procurement; own the readiness cadence end to end.
Scope hub-to-spoke routing opportunities — Build the business case for hub-sort-to-spoke direct routing and bring recommendations forward to Network Design and Real Estate.
Close forecasting product gaps — Identify where forecasting tools fail to capture capacity reality and drive the fix with Data/Product partners.
Own Mx launch — Own Mx launch end to end, including CET allocation by merchant priority, negotiating trade-offs across competing merchant demands.
You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
3-6-12 month runway visibility ahead of any projected capacity constraint.
Site launch recommendations delivered proactively, not reactively.
% of high-priority Mx launches assigned an optimal CET.
We're excited about you because you have…
Strategic model ownership — You've built and owned a capacity, forecasting, or network constraint model that became a standing input to planning — not a one-off analysis.
Independent judgment — You can independently judge where the real bottleneck is across a large, multi-site network, without a pre-scoped problem statement.
Cross-functional negotiation — You've negotiated trade-off recommendations with senior, cross-functional stakeholders (e.g., Network Design, Real Estate, Finance) and influenced capital-adjacent decisions.
Physical operations fluency — You understand physical warehouse operations deeply enough to translate dock, floor, throughput, and labor constraints into a single model.
Experience — 7+ years in supply chain, network strategy, or operations, with direct experience owning capacity planning or site launch strategy at scale.

Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the Customer Success team:
Customer Success is dedicated to enabling our customers to get the most out of the automation we deploy, facilitating a superb experience through all facets of our relationship. We are manufacturing and automation experts–consulting with customers to drive adoption and optimal usage of our robotic automation solutions, and identifying opportunities to continue their automation journey.
As Customer Success Manager , you will serve as the primary point of contact and advisory partner for our customers: visiting and consulting with those customers in the field, and driving solutions across various groups within Formic for optimal delivery of technical, operational, training and administrative support for our industrial robot systems.
You will play a key role in driving mutually beneficial customer relationships post-deployment by monitoring customer health and engagement, mitigating potential relationship and experience risks, and identifying growth opportunities in existing accounts. You will build and maintain strong customer relationships; develop a deep understanding of their business goals, challenges, and needs; and will leverage that feedback to provide customized insights and value-added products and services. This position is highly strategic and impactful in Formic’s mission to be a valued partner and leader driving the adoption of automation across the manufacturing industry.
Internally, you will act as the voice of the customer within Formic, delivering feedback and recommendations internally to drive product and process improvements to yield better outcomes and experience. You will be instrumental in equipping Formic’s various teams to consistently deliver high performance automation solutions with superb customer experience.
As Customer Success Manager, you will:
Serve as the primary consultative partner and point of contact for the group of customers you are responsible for: building strong relationships; facilitating technical, operational, training, and administrative support; and identifying opportunities for expansion.
Oversee a regular cadence of communication and site visits (including regular travel throughout your region) to assess satisfaction with deployed robotic automation systems, address relationship issues, facilitate and offer training, solicit feedback, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.
Monitor & manage health and engagement by using diagnostic tools and strategic communication, identifying and mitigating potential relationship and experience risks.
Collaborate with Formic’s Sales, Deployment, and Service teams to guide customers - particularly first time automation buyers - through their automation journey.
Identify opportunities for growth of products and services within existing accounts, including deployment of additional like-for-like solutions, or upstream or downstream standard solutions.
Leverage understanding of customers’ businesses to provide feedback for new product offerings and service enhancements for Formic to better serve their needs.
What makes you a great fit:
3-5+ years of experience in a manufacturing operations role (e.g. Plant or Production Manager/Supervisor/Process Engineering Leader) in a manufacturing or production operations environment.
Familiarity with robotic automation systems in a manufacturing or production environment (e.g. robotic automation of palletizing, de-palletizing, case packing, machine tending, welding, injection molding).
Outstanding communication and stakeholder management skills–able to build trusting relationships with diverse stakeholders and audiences and collaborate cross-functionally
Strong judgment and calm execution during escalations, shifting priorities, and time-sensitive customer needs
Ability to identify expansion opportunities through strong relationships, customer insight, and operational outcomes
Proficiency with CRM and customer relationship management tools such as Salesforce, ticketing systems, or project tracking platforms
Strong operational discipline, follow-through, and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
Experience working with industrial, manufacturing, hardware, robotics, or operationally complex customers preferred
Experience working successfully with a portfolio of industrial automation users leading to adoption, expansion and renewals preferred–ideally of technical platforms and solutions
Consultative sales experience is a plus
Ability to travel ~30% of the time to customer sites across their region, living in close proximity to a major airport
Holding a current, valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle
What we look for:
We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!
Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

title: ASIC Power Engineer, ML Accelerators
description:
In this role, you’ll work to shape the future of AI/ML hardware acceleration. You will have an opportunity to drive cutting-edge TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) technology that powers Google's most demanding AI/ML applications. You’ll be part of a team that pushes boundaries, developing custom silicon solutions that power the future of Google's TPU. You'll contribute to the innovation behind products loved by millions worldwide, and leverage your design and verification expertise to verify complex digital designs, with a specific focus on TPU architecture and its integration within AI/ML-driven systems.
As part of the TPU power design team, you will play a pivotal part in improving the power efficiency of our TPUs. You will drive power efficiency for our TPU designs, starting from building power models to proposing novel power optimization techniques. You would possess a deep background in modeling and optimizing chip power, as well as have an understanding of system level power considerations and tradeoffs.
As an ASIC Design Engineer, you will be part of a team developing ASICs used to accelerate computation in data centers. You will have dynamic, multi-faceted responsibilities in areas such as project definition, design, and implementation. You will participate in the design, architecture, documentation, and implementation of the next generation of data center accelerators. The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.
We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
US: $163000 - $236000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits
Learn more about benefits at Google .

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
8 years of experience in silicon design or architecture (e.g., logic design, power architecture, performance, or SoC design).

title: Analyst, Geospatial (GIS)
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
Invenergy is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Geospatial Analyst to join our collaborative E ngineering & GIS tea m. This entry-level role is perfect for individuals eager to grow their technical skills while learning how geospatial data drives decisions across energy project lifecycles.
As a Geospatial Analyst, you wil l gain valuable experience supporting projects that power homes and businesses . You will learn not only technical GIS workflows but also how those workflows fit into the broader development process—giving you insight into multiple aspects of the energy business. This role is an excellent foundation for advancing into a specialist, developer, or project-focused roles while making a meaningful impact as you learn how energy infrastructure projects are built.
As a Geospatial Analyst, you will be part of a team that supports multiple departments—Development, Engineering, Environmental, and Land—ensuring geospatial data and mapping are accurate , accessible, and useful. You’ll gain exposure to many aspects of the business process, from project siting and permitting to construction and operations.
Key Responsibilities
Collaborative Mapping & Data Support
Work closely with GIS Analysts and Developers to deliv er high-quality maps , data, and interactive, online products .
Partner with Development and Engineering teams to meet project needs and deadlines.
Incorporate feedback from multiple stakeholders to refine deliverables.
Project & Workflow Support
Assist with map requests, spatial data integration, and basic analyses.
Support project intake by organizing surveys , parcels , and environmental datasets.
Learn how geospatial workflows contribute to siting, land acquisition, permitting, and design.
Data Management & Learning
Maintain centralized GIS databases with attention to standards and version control.

Job Description:
Job: Production Leader
Shift: Nights
Location: Mars (Topeka, KS)
The Production Leader is a shift-based, front-line operations people Manager who efficiently improves Quality, Human Safety, and Product Cost Conversion while Engaging and Developing talent. The Production Leader is responsible for delivering operational targets and leading teams of, on average, 15 Shift associates.  The Production Leader drives safety, quality, continuous improvement, performance management, associate development, team engagement, and operating results for their assigned area through shift-based leadership of a line or area that exists within a larger Value Stream organization.
This leader coordinate the short-term activities of the area within established guidelines and standards to produce the highest quality, lowest cost product most safely and efficiently while also partnering with the other members of the 24-hour Area Managership Team to deliver area continuous improvement and Mars Supply Excellence (MSE) program implementation. The Production Leader is responsible for building an effective team on his/her shift and in his/her area of responsibility and for managing the training strategy for both the individual associates and the team. This leader will implement and enforce established policy and area and organizational strategies.
Key Responsibilities:
Conversion - Manage the efforts of multi-line, area, or technology operating teams on one shift to efficiently convert materials into quality products in a safe, secure, and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.
Change Agent - Implement changes in methods, equipment, systems, and organization, as needed, to ensure that the objectives of the line/area are met and give input and recommendations for such changes by using a continuous improvement mindset.
Mars Supply Excellence – Lead or participate in one or more MSE Pillars; Lead and support the implementation of Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs) in area of responsibility; Lead key connection points and own reliability data collection accuracy.
Area Ownership – Collaborate with the rest of the Area Managership Team (Area Manager or Continuous Improvement Engineer, Continuous Improvement Specialist, Maintenance Coordinator) to create and execute the reliability strategy for the area of responsibility.
Coaching—Coach operators to build their functional and Managerial capabilities and drive accountability in safety, Quality and Food Safety, Autonomous Maintenance, and team engagement.
Line Operations - Coordinate materials, staffing, and resources to support line operation and changeovers.
Standards Implementation and Adherence – Ensure standards are implemented on shift and in areas of responsibility through effective communication, change management, consistent reinforcement, coaching, guidance, and accountability measures.
Associate Safety – Ensure safe working conditions, behaviors, and mindsets through the direct implementation of Mars Safety programs and driving a relentless focus among a team of operators.
Food Safety and Product Quality – Ensure the ongoing Shift of safe and defect-free products consistent with the principles of Mars.  HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Associate Advocacy - Manage associate relations issues and guide and direct the hiring, training, retraining, development, and motivation of Operations associates following self-managed, team-working principles with a minimum degree of guidance from the Area Manager or Value Stream Manager.

Goal Setting and Measurement - With the general guidance of the Value Stream or Area Manager and/or the support of the Continuous Improvement Engineer, establish line and individual performance standards and goals, and measure, control, take corrective action, and report results as appropriate.
Troubleshooting – Utilize the technical resources on shift for the preventive maintenance, repair and troubleshooting of process/packaging equipment problems, to effectively use these resources to achieve desired performance levels.
Escalations - Proactively identify risks and opportunities and reactively lead on-shift incident resolution when operators require additional support. Prioritize, assign resources against escalated issues, and make decisions to resolve escalated issues.
Communications - Ensure that open communications are established and that opportunities to broaden the scope and responsibility of Operations teams/associates are undertaken.
Technology Advancement - Advise when opportunities exist for moving the line/area forward in technological change.
Operations Strategy - Participate in implementing improvement strategies to help the line/area perform more effectively in the near term.

We are seeking an employment lawyer to help build the legal foundations for OpenAI’s next stage of growth. Working closely with our employment counsel team and colleagues across the company, you will shape practical approaches to challenging employment issues in a fast-growing AI company. This is a hands-on role for a thoughtful lawyer who enjoys variety, moves quickly, and wants to help build a strong employment legal function as the business scales.



You will collaborate with experienced employment counsel on US and international employment issues, the employment aspects of mergers and acquisitions, and emerging questions about AI in the workplace. A central part of your work will be turning lessons from individual matters into practical policies, guidance, and approaches that work at scale. You will also own stakeholder relationships and manage counseling matters, exercising sound judgment and taking responsibility for outcomes. You will join a bright, collaborative team that values initiative and shared learning, with opportunities to learn from senior colleagues, deepen your expertise, and take on increasingly complex matters over time.

title: Data Center Electrical R&D Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is building the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The team defines the technical direction for next-generation data centers and develops the architectures needed to support rapidly evolving AI hardware and workload requirements.

Operating at the intersection of research, engineering, infrastructure, and deployment, the team translates emerging compute requirements into validated electrical designs, reference architectures, prototypes, and scalable infrastructure solutions.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Data Center Electrical R&D Engineer to develop and validate next-generation power architectures for high-density AI infrastructure.

This role is focused on research, advanced design, modeling, prototyping, and technical validation rather than ongoing facility operations. You will investigate emerging electrical technologies, develop system-level architectures, and evaluate new approaches to utility integration, power distribution, backup generation, energy storage, controls, and rack-level power delivery.

You will work closely with compute hardware, mechanical, controls, construction, commissioning, operations, and external technology partners. Your work will shape reusable reference designs that can move from concept and simulation through pilot testing and large-scale deployment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop advanced electrical architectures for high-density AI data centers, from utility interconnection through rack-level power delivery.

 - Translate evolving compute-platform requirements into electrical capacity, topology, redundancy, power-quality, protection, and control requirements.

 - Create conceptual designs, basis-of-design documents, specifications, one-line diagrams, design standards, and reusable reference architectures.

 - Model electrical-system performance, capacity, efficiency, reliability, fault conditions, transient behavior, and failure scenarios.

 - Evaluate emerging technologies such as medium-voltage distribution, solid-state power conversion, advanced UPS systems, energy storage, alternative generation, and direct-current architectures.

 - Build technical and economic comparisons across competing design approaches, including reliability, efficiency, scalability, cost, constructability, maintainability, and deployment speed.

 - Develop prototypes, test plans, acceptance criteria, and validation frameworks for new electrical technologies and system architectures.

 - Lead laboratory, factory, pilot-site, and field testing to validate design assumptions and identify performance or integration gaps.

 - Partner with mechanical and thermal engineers to optimize power and cooling architectures as an integrated system.

 - Collaborate with AI hardware and compute teams to understand workload behavior, rack density, utilization, power variability, and future platform requirements.

 - Work with controls and software teams to define instrumentation, telemetry, protection, monitoring, and automated-control requirements.

 - Partner with construction, commissioning, and operations teams to ensure new designs can be safely built, tested, operated, and maintained.

 - Engage equipment manufacturers, utilities, engineering consultants, and research partners to evaluate capabilities and accelerate technology development.

 - Investigate system failures and unexpected test results, identify root causes, and translate findings into design improvements.

 - Document validated designs, technical decisions, operating envelopes, lessons learned, and deployment guidance.

 - Provide technical direction and design-review leadership across internal teams and external engineering partners.

 - 10+ years of experience in electrical engineering, power-system design, data-center infrastructure, industrial power, or another critical-infrastructure environment.

 - Demonstrated experience developing electrical designs for large, complex, or high-availability facilities.

 - Strong understanding of power-system modeling, short-circuit analysis, load flow, coordination studies, arc-flash analysis, power quality, grounding, and reliability.

 - Experience translating uncertain or evolving technical requirements into testable engineering concepts and system architectures.

 - Experience designing experiments, prototypes, pilots, or validation programs for new equipment or infrastructure technologies.

 - Ability to reason across electrical, mechanical, controls, compute hardware, construction, commissioning, and operational boundaries.

 - Strong technical writing and communication skills, including the ability to explain complex engineering decisions to technical and executive audiences.

 - Experience directing engineering consultants, equipment manufacturers, and external technology partners.

 - Master’s degree or PhD in electrical engineering, power systems, power electronics, energy systems, or a related field.

 - Professional Engineer license or equivalent professional certification.

 - Experience supporting high-density data centers, AI infrastructure, semiconductor manufacturing, advanced industrial facilities, or hyperscale computing environments.

 - Experience with ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, PSCAD, MATLAB/Simulink, or comparable power-system analysis tools.

 - Experience with power electronics, energy storage, microgrids, alternative generation, or advanced grid-interconnection technologies.

 - Familiarity with digital twins, hardware-in-the-loop testing, real-time simulation, and data-driven infrastructure optimization.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

Business Marketing helps organizations understand and put OpenAI’s products to work. Our creative team brings that story to life across campaigns, launches, and everyday marketing experiences. We work closely with marketing partners to make ambitious, thoughtful creative work that connects with business audiences.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Events Designer to create memorable visual experiences across OpenAI events, live streams, and global product announcements. You’ll develop cohesive visual identities and translate them across keynote presentations, large-format screens, streaming graphics, event environments, and merchandise. Working closely with brand, marketing, events, motion, and production teams, you’ll bring strong creative thinking and hands-on design craft to every experience.

In this role, you will

 - Design event experiences from concept to execution, including signage, wayfinding, wall graphics, apparel, merchandise, and other onsite brand applications.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

 - Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

 - Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

 - Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

 - Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

 - Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

 - Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

 - Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

 - Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

 - Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

 - Lead recurring product-cost and TCO reviews. Publish concise cost bridges, opportunity updates, risks, and decision packages while retaining the supporting detail needed for technical and financial review.

 - Build scalable models, reporting, and data workflows that improve baseline completeness, refresh speed, analysis turnaround, and decision quality as the hardware portfolio grows.

 - You will own integrated product economics and the cost-analysis methodology and the cost analysis itself. Strategic Sourcing and manufacturing-partner management retain commercial negotiations; Engineering retains design and qualification authority; DC and site teams own their source inputs; Finance retains budgets, accounting, and financial approvals; Planning owns the demand baseline; SCPM owns material readiness; and OPM owns operational execution.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Significant experience in hardware product costing, cost engineering, supply chain finance, manufacturing cost analysis, or a related role supporting complex technology products.

 - Experience building and maintaining multi-level costed BOMs, system cost roll-ups, and lifecycle or TCO models across product development, production ramp, and sustaining operations.

 - Strong understanding of hardware cost drivers, including component pricing, manufacturing labor and overhead, NRE, tooling, yield, scrap, test, logistics, and service costs.

 - Demonstrated ability to evaluate engineering changes, second-source options, and cost-reduction opportunities using comparable scenarios and transparent assumptions.

 - Advanced spreadsheet and quantitative modeling skills, with disciplined data reconciliation, version control, and source traceability.

 - Ability to turn incomplete or changing technical and commercial inputs into defensible analysis, identify uncertainty, and drive input gaps to closure.

 - Strong cross-functional influence and communication skills, including concise leadership recommendations and detailed working sessions with engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and finance teams.

 - High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements and competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centers, custom silicon, servers, networking, storage, or rack-scale systems.

 - Experience analyzing JDM, CM, or ODM cost structures and open-book manufacturing models.

 - Familiarity with DC and site economics, power and cooling, deployment timing, spares, and service costs in infrastructure TCO.

 - Experience with ERP, MRP, and PLM systems, BOM change control, and business intelligence or automation/AI tools.

 - A background in engineering, finance, supply chain, manufacturing, or a related analytical discipline.

 - Teams use a complete, current, and traceable costed BOM and system/pod baseline as the source of truth for product economics.

 - Platform TCO comparisons use consistent scope and assumptions, with inputs validated by their owners.

 - Material engineering and sourcing decisions include timely cost-impact analysis and explicit tradeoffs.

 - Cost variances have clear explanations, accountable owners, and recovery actions; savings and cost avoidance are validated.
